reviews.title: BEWARE
reviews.text: I downloaded BOOM app for iOS from the App Store to my iPad. The app functions and works with Apple Music on my old MacBook Pro, so when I completed the download for iOS, I went ahead and purchased the lifetime BOOM membership for $20. Well, BOHICA!!! There ought to be a disclaimer when purchasing or downloading the app that its functionality with Apple Music is compromised by DRM restrictions. “Due to DRM restrictions you cannot apply any Boom effects on Apple Music streams or downloaded tracks.” Searching the community, it’s pretty obvious that I’m not the first Apple customer to encounter this problem, so it is also apparent that Apple is aware of this problem. My first question: Why is this an issue with iOS and not on Mac OS? My second question is: If Apple is aware of this issue (and you know they are) why don’t they tell us about it when you prepare to download the Boom app or make ”in app purchases?” I’m out $20 for a whole lot of nothing. Why would I need the Boom app for anything other than my streaming and downloaded content from Apple Music? Even if I can seamlessly use Boom with other apps, my entire music library (including music I purchased pre-Apple) is in Apple Music library along with other purchased content. Last question: since Apple owns just about everything else, can they own responsibility for their customers being taken for their hard earned cash? (here, I am giving the app a one star rating. On my MacBook Pro I would give it a 4 or 5 star review.)

reviews.title: Mix Review
reviews.text: If you have all your music from Apple then this is likely a very functional app. If your music was not purchased from Apple this app is not what you want. I use other third party apps to play non Apple music and they all create their own local folder on my iPad and then it’s easy to add media to the folder and access my entire collection. When you share a song to the Boom app, which you have to do by individual song, you can’t find where the song is stored anywhere on your iOS device. If this app allowed you to access entire folders of music stored on your iOS device it would be awesome but it does not. I do love the Mac version of the Boom app and will continue to use that. If there is a way for the developer to contact me when they allow access to music folders on iOS I would love that as I will continue not to use the app until that happens.
